subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, scope, and privacy rules should it use relative to user-token `search.messages`?
rationale: The feature is valid but security-sensitive because it would handle event-scoped Slack action tokens and workspace-wide search results, and the adjacent user-token search attempts do not settle the assistant-token contract.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, redaction, rate-limit handling, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Define one Slack search contract that covers RTS and user-token `search.messages`, then revive or replace the closed search/action-parity work against that design.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep Slack RTS out of OpenClaw until maintainers are ready to own the token/privacy/scope model and live validation burden.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, redaction, rate-limit handling, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is recent ownership of Slack assistant-thread lifecycle and the broad Slack action-parity attempt touching the same action surfaces.
